biggest_catch: Quicktate officially requires YOU to pay a $20 background-check fee before you can get any work ('You agree to pay the $20 cost of the background check'), while publishing no pay rate, pay method, or pay schedule anywhere on its official transcriber page — so you pay out of pocket with no official figure for what you will earn.
catches: Upfront cost: the official signup page requires you to pay the $20 background-check fee (PayPal or credit card) after passing the quiz and typing test — you pay before receiving any assignments.

No official pay rate is published: the official page only says 'I agree to deliver the transcription to Company at the pricing agreed to in advance' — the $0.0025/word figure appears only in third-party sources and could NOT be confirmed officially.
Zero guaranteed tasks: you are an independent contractor and 'do not have the right to be offered' future assignments; each file is one assignment, accepted or rejected individually.

You must pass the Quicktate quiz, a typing quiz for each language/specialty, and a requirements test; provide 3 non-family references; and have no felony or misdemeanor convictions ('Do not proceed if you have ever been convicted').
Variable task availability: work consists of short voicemail/memo/phone-call files; nothing guarantees volume.

Effective hourly pay can be low: with no official rate, third-party worker reports describe very low effective hourly pay (one worker cited ~$1/hour) — unconfirmed officially, but the absence of any published rate is itself the risk.
You must supply all your own equipment, facilities, software, and supplies, and agree to the HIPAA Business Associate Agreement.

c1.evidence: Quicktate (with sister company iDictate) — real transcription company transcribing voicemail, memos, legal/medical files, and phone calls; official transcriber portal at typists.quicktate.com.

c2.evidence: Official transcriber signup page (typists.quicktate.com/transcribers/signup) confirms the typist/contractor opportunity with an 8-step qualification flow: account, agreements, quiz, specialty test, references, paid background check, gov't ID verification, results.

c3.evidence: Upfront cost is disclosed officially: 'Background Checks: After you pass the Quiz and the typing test, we will run a background check on you. You agree to pay the $20 cost of the background check. This may be paid using PayPal or credit card.' — a mandatory $20 fee before any work, so upfront_fee=true.

c4.evidence: No official Quicktate page publishes any pay figure or pay mechanism: no per-word rate, no payment method, no pay schedule on the official signup page. The widely cited $0.0025/word rate and weekly PayPal payments appear only in third-party reviews, never officially.

eligibility: Official: no felony or misdemeanor convictions (do not apply if ever convicted); typists with own equipment, supplies, and facilities; must pass the Quicktate quiz, a typing quiz per language/specialty, and the requirements test; must provide three non-family references; must pass the paid background check and government ID verification; must agree to the Typist Handbook, policies, confidentiality agreement, and HIPAA Business Associate Agreement. Open to non-US applicants (country field on the form; tax ID referenced by third parties, not confirmed officially).

The task's '$0.0025/word-ish rate' was NOT found on any official page. Catalog $0 claim has no official figure to check against.
